summary:
Our project is an interactive Roblox game designed to train students in managing a Martian outpost through real-world space mission trade-offs. Structured across five progressive acts, the game gradually guides players from simple single-system puzzles to high-stakes simulations where they must manage oxygen, radiation shielding, power, and food production simultaneously. During crises like dust storms, solar flares, and freezing temperatures, players allocate limited power and crew members while applying practical problem-solving skills learned in earlier levels.
This project addresses the challenge by turning complex aerospace engineering trade-offs into hands-on, accessible gameplay rather than overly technical lessons or oversimplified trivia. By gradually increasing difficulty and weaving in relatable, story-driven challenges, it keeps young learners actively engaged while teaching the consequences of every resource decision.
This mission trainer is important because it builds critical thinking, systems thinking, and STEM confidence in youth. Hosting the experience on Roblox makes space education widely accessible, empowering students everywhere to experience firsthand how real astronauts and engineers balance competing demands to keep a mission alive.
details: Missions on Mars take place on a Martian outpost during the climax of Estelle’s career as a veteran commander, challenging players to survive a catastrophic four-day crisis loop. Players must monitor four continuously draining survival meters ranging from 0 to 100: Oxygen, Radiation Shielding, Power, and Food Production. If any meter drops to zero, the crew is placed in immediate danger. Because electricity is shared across the entire base, every emergency forces difficult strategic trade-offs where diverting power to rescue one failing system leaves another vulnerable, requiring players to constantly weigh risks and prioritize competing needs. Set entirely during a massive Martian dust storm, the mission throws all four life-threatening crises at the crew simultaneously. Thin, dusty air clogs the life-support filtration system, a major solar storm strikes with almost no warning, swirling dust blocks sunlight from reaching the solar panels, and greenhouse crops begin to fail in the extreme cold. To survive, Estelle and the elders must trust the young trainees and apply practical survival lessons learned earlier on Earth—using bottle-garden techniques to rescue failing crops, school-grade filtration methods to clear clogged air scrubbers, and blackout drills to ration dwindling power room by room. When the Martian base successfully endures the storm, the signal is heard back in Sarawak by a child on a rooftop, passing the star-chart and the spirit of space exploration to the next generation of dreamers. Built in Roblox Studio using Luau scripting, the game combines custom user interface gauges, timed emergency triggers, and interactive habitat modules to simulate real-time resource depletion and high-pressure decision-making. By connecting relatable local roots in Sarawak with real aerospace engineering challenges—including closed-loop life support, radiation shielding, solar power constraints, and controlled-environment agriculture—Lunará Estellé demonstrates that big decisions in space are built from small survival lessons learned on Earth.
